title: [CQ-M03c] defect workload fixtures
description: Objective: Freeze five distinct defect workloads for the 20-case CQ-M03 matched corpus. Deliverable: packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.ts and defectWorkloads.test.ts, exporting this category's frozen dataset using the M03a workloadSnapshot contract. Frozen corpus contract (version 1): each workload has a unique category-prefixed id, category (maintenance/defect/refactor/non-routine), full startingCommit 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71, named repo source provenance, intendedBehavior/task instructions, deterministic snapshot digest over a documented sorted-path/UTF-8-byte encoding, initialFiles and separately held-out assessmentFiles (relative portable paths mapped to immutable UTF-8 strings), and explicit assessment rubric criteria/coverage tags. assessmentFiles contains executable independent black-box acceptance tests; it must not be copied into the coding snapshot. Include bounded reviewable Node ESM fixture source adaptations grounded in original Moe source, not twenty renamed toy cases, and label any reduced/adapted snapshot provenance honestly. No reference solution in coding inputs. Every case has a concrete original-state failure/required change and unchanged-acceptance positive and adversarial-negative controls; no agent judge/price/network dependency. The shared materializer owns only newly created os.tmpdir directories and offers fresh reset by new snapshot creation, never an arbitrary target root or Git reset/worktree operation. Category boundary: Five cases: stale-positive context claims a helper/export exists after the frozen source removed it; stale-negative context claims no helper exists although the frozen source added it (require reuse, no duplicate); a changed caller passes a new input shape and old cached signature breaks; changed requirements require a different explicit policy outcome than stale notes recommend; a stored verification recipe is incompatible with the declared platform/runtime and must be rejected/replaced rather than executed optimistically (recipe-mismatch tag). Ground in actual bounded context, normalization, execution-profile and cached-path patterns. Include stale artifacts as inert data with separate source provenance and independent expected behavior; do not invent a production context API. Keep all fixture payloads/test-only corrected and plausible-wrong variants in these two files; no production edits, benchmark runs, aggregate corpus edits or edits to the dependency. Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts
definitionOfDone: Exactly five distinct defect fixtures validate against landed M03a contract, with frozen full starting commit, source provenance, intended behavior, content hashes and independent executable acceptance rubrics.

Each fixture has an unsolved original that fails at least one intended-change criterion, a test-only corrected variant passing the same unchanged rubric, and a plausible wrong variant rejected by it; no reference solution or assessment bytes enter coding inputs.

Cases retain category-specific invariants and explicit context/helper/caller/requirements/recipe coverage tags where applicable; snapshots and repeated resets are deterministic and never alter source checkout bytes.
Fresh cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits or Git-write commands; wrappers own landing. Preserve all peer/pre-existing dirty bytes.
Frozen benchmark/test scaffolding only; do not alter production behavior, enable verified-local, or claim VM/isolation certification.
Do not edit sibling category datasets/tests, the shared contract after it lands, or the M03 assembler; use explicit dependency updates for any contract change.

  - Bounded-context budget: a changed chat-budget caller.

- **Stale context is shipped as inert files.** Each lives under context/ or recipes/, carries a staleness header and provenance, and is never imported. Rubrics are independent of the artifacts, and a test proves the corrected variant passes even with the artifact deleted.

planningNotes.risks:
- **Vacuous controls:** a crash or syntax error must never count as a correct rejection. The wrong variant must fail the NAMED criterion, and the corrected variant must report every criterion id as ok.
- **Case 1 env:** the assessment must set MOE_EXECUTION_PROFILE_READY before dynamically importing the candidate. The spawned process starts from process.env, so nothing leaks back into vitest.
- **Case 5 executes nothing:** it must not run anything real. Only the injected exec spy may be called; never spawn pwsh/bun/node from the fixture.
- **Honest deviations:** case 4 deliberately re-introduces a superseded branch, and case 5's selector is synthetic. Both notes must say so, and neither fixture may claim to be a whole-repository snapshot.
- **Template-literal escaping:** fixture JS with backslashes, backticks or `${` needs `\\`, a backslash before each backtick, and `\${`.
- **Forbidden patterns:** the project's global forbiddenPatterns are raw substring checks that also apply to fixture strings and to longer identifiers. Avoid them all.
- **Dependency:** M03a is unlanded at planning time. Wait for DONE and adapt to its real exports without editing it.
- **Repo hygiene:** no production edits, no Git/.moe writes, and preserve the shared tree's peer/pre-existing dirty bytes. Focused runs only; one final gate.
